messages.author: 0a92b47c1c513471
messages.subject: POST form data with multiple values for one variable
parts:
Hello,

I have an R script that performs a t-test. I would like to input data
such that the POST variable is like a data frame, with columns for
every variable (like mean, sd, sample size) for each group.

Right now I am getting the data like this:

<form method="POST" action="">
<input type="hidden" name="type" value="ttest">
Mean 1: <input type="text" name="mean1">
SD 1: <input type="text" name="sd1">
N1: <input type="text" name="n1"><br /><br />
Mean 2: <input type="text" name="mean2">
SD 2: <input type="text" name="sd2">
N2: <input type="text" name="n2"><br /><br />
<P>
<INPUT TYPE=RADIO NAME="pooled" VALUE="pooled">pooled<BR>
<INPUT TYPE=RADIO NAME="pooled" VALUE="unpooled">unpooled<P>
<input type=submit name="Submit" value = "Get Results!">
</form>
and str(POST) returns

List of 9
$ type : chr "ttest"
$ mean1 : chr "5"
$ sd1 : chr "5"
$ n1 : chr "5"
$ mean2 : chr "5"
$ sd2 : chr "5"
$ n2 : chr "5"
$ pooled: chr "pooled"
$ Submit: chr "Get Results!"

I then reference the POST$p1 for mean, etc. But this method only
allows me to compare two groups at a time. I would like to have it so
that POST is a data frame with variables for mean1, mean 2, etc and
each row would be two groups that I want to compare. So then calling
my t_test function would look like:

t_test(POST$mean1[1], POST$mean2[1]....)


Is there any way to do this, preferably similar to how I am doing the
single comparison now, but not necessarily if my way is completely
wrong :D ?

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: POST form data with multiple values for one variable
parts:
You should upgrade your R installation in order to get up-to-date packages. Why would you choose RJSONIO over rjson - that one's easy: speed. RJSONIO is faster (at least they advertise so in official documentation). AFAIK RJSONIO was hosted on omegahat before it was uploaded on CRAN, so all you have to do is to grab gzipped tarball and install package from local hard drive.

Take a look at http://www.omegahat.org/RJSONIO/
Once you download the package archive, run:
install.packages("<pkg name>", type = "source", repos = NULL)

but you should really update your R installation, since RJSONIO is now on CRAN. Basic functionallity is pretty similar: toJSON() and fromJSON() methods exist in both packages.

About data structure: keep in mind that RApache provides POST superglobal, much like PHP. It is a list. All you have to do is to tweak the list, or (even better) tweak the data on the client side. You may want to use some JS library. My choice is jQuery. Take a look at jQuery form plugin: http://jquery.malsup.com/form/ - this should be helpful

Or you can use vanilla jQuery. In a nutshell, you should pass POST parameters as JSON string - i.e. you should encode them before you submit the form, then decode/deparse the JSON string on the server side.

So there... That's pretty much it.

Good luck! =)
